arms.better: tm created T-1 clearly and initially found the right decoder, but each attempt reread the same decoder/tests and searched the same BOM/TrimPrefix concepts without stating a plan or making an edit. Attempts stopped at the 10-step no-progress threshold, consumed 169,493, 192,011, and 205,213 reported tokens, and the final run escalated without running tests or submitting a patch. The user-facing recovery text recommends resuming S-3 and then says to run `tm ticket retry T-1`, while the log also says a retry is scheduled; that leaves unclear whether any action is needed and whether prior investigation will be reused. A single constrained continuation grounded in the already identified UnmarshalToMap target, aggregate retry token/time accounting, and one unambiguous terminal/retry status would have made the run useful and substantially cheaper. The PR test-file checkout followed by `go test ./parser/metadecoders/...` passed, but this independent check does not demonstrate a TM-authored fix.

OpenCode located UnmarshalToMap and its table-driven test, stated the minimal plan, stripped the BOM and added TOML/YAML/JSON cases. It transparently noted that the earlier Unmarshal behavior was not present at this base SHA, then used the explicit BOM bytes. `./check.sh ./parser/metadecoders/...` passed, and its final report accurately described the code and checks. A semantic-index lookup failed because the disposable clone had no index, but it switched immediately to exact search and continued without wasting the run. It could be slightly more efficient by avoiding the initial unavailable index probe and could add a targeted config-loading regression as described in the issue; its parser tests cover all three affected formats directly.
